LESSON: RECORDING SKILLS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.1: Recording skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Recording skills, part of Writing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: What do we wear on a rainy day?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. observe different weather conditions during the day,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Recording skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. tell difference between weather conditions observed,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Recording skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. record observed weather conditions in a simple weather chart,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Recording skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. actively participate in activities involving reporting or recording observations. ● Observe different weather conditions on a video clip or chart. Light intensity be adjusted for those who are sensitive to light ● Observe weather conditions outside the classroom during a nature walk. Learners with mobility difficulties to be supported by peers to move. ● Identify pictures on weather symbols such as rainy, windy, sunny and cloudy from charts and books, ● Tick weather symbol observed on a chart on the particular day, (the weather chart should have 5 days of a week, from Monday to Friday and the four weather conditions symbols for morning session and afternoon session. The learner should tick one symbol every morning after observation and one symbol every afternoon What do we wear on a rainy day? 78 on the same day after observing weather for the 5 day

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Recording skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Unity: The learner works cooperatively with others to record the weather chart.

• Responsibility: The learner records the weather chart persistently for a week.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. observe different weather conditions during the day,
2. tell difference between weather conditions observed,
3. record observed weather conditions in a simple weather chart,
4. actively participate in activities involving reporting or recording observations. ● Observe different weather conditions on a video clip or chart. Light intensity be adjusted for those who are sensitive to light ● Observe weather conditions outside the classroom during a nature walk. The learner should tick one symbol every morning after observation and one symbol every afternoon What do we wear on a rainy day? 78 on the same day after observing weather for the 5 day
5. . Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools or appropriate digital devices to tick weather symbols. ● Display recorded weather charts at the end of the week. Learners with manipulation difficulties could be supported by peers to display their work

Core competencies:

• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner objectively records the weather chart on a daily basis after observation.

• Self-efficacy: The learner confidently displays the recorded weather chart for others to view and peer assess.

Values:

• Unity: The learner works cooperatively with others to record the weather chart.

• Responsibility: The learner records the weather chart persistently for a week.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issue(
s) :

Social cohesion: The learner interacts with others where they do consultation in recording observed weather.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Recording observed weather is linked to Environmental Activities where the learner learns about weather symbols.
